dedupe_keys.name: gis based hourly model of renewable hydrogen production potential for 62 mediterranean ports

description: This model, published by Giovanni Battista Barone, Giovanni Francesco Giuzio, Robert Maka, Adolfo Palombo and Giuseppe Russo of the University of Naples Federico II in Energy Conversion and Management (2026), assesses the hydrogen production potential of 62 ports in the Mediterranean with a Geographic Information System framework. Coverage: solar, wind and wave energy at each port, coupled with battery storage to supply electrolysis, simulated hourly to capture variable generation, storage operation, electrolyser sizing and control, and grid interaction, in fully renewable and hybrid configurations. Solar gives capacity factors of about 18% to 24%, wind reaches close to 30% at some ports, and wave energy has limited viability. The levelised cost of hydrogen is about 5.7 to 8.6 EUR per kg fully renewable and 2.5 to over 13 EUR per kg in hybrid systems, depending on grid prices and emission intensities. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the code is not described in the abstract, which was the part read. The port-by-port resource and cost results can set local renewable potential and electrolyser capacity in port energy hub and capacity planning models. It relates to the Global Solar Atlas and the IEA hydrogen projects database in the catalogue.
